rows.reason: Borland C++ run-time: floating-point emulator (INT 34h-3Dh), float-to-text conversion, far-heap allocator, file and exit chain, overlay manager (INT 3Fh, EMS INT 67h); read in decompiled/dos-2.0.1/all.c, the routine read with its calls, and the bytes of DOSHO.EXE scanned for the data-segment offsets of its literal strings (the strings named below are the ones found). rows.shows: On a crash, a line of text in the DOS screen: Null pointer assignment, Divide error, Abnormal program termination.
rows.reason: The Borland C++ run-time's abnormal-termination text ("Null pointer assignment", "Divide error", "Abnormal program termination"), written to DOS when the program ends badly (the label names are the strings; read in decompiled/dos-2.0.1/all.c (private repo)). A web page has no process to end.

rows.shows: A developer's trace or assertion line; not part of normal play.
rows.reason: A debugging line of the program's own checks ("Fleet not at star", "bad galnum in getplayerstarnum", "big initialization problem", "CalcOneGroup average is %d ...", "total of %d type %d ships power", "want to build %d at cost of %ld", "Going to explore %s from %s ...", "scrapping colony ship fleet %d", "bad percTotal %d", "num left is %d", "Etpower for pl %d at %d is %d"): printed only when a rule check fails or a developer's trace is on; not part of a game. The computer players' choices these lines trace are the ones the ruleset reads (docs/dos-findings.md).

Read in decompiled/dos-2.0.1/all.c (private repo) with every call followed (FUN_ and func_0x calls resolved to routines, 1,964 of them): no path from this routine reaches a routine that writes video memory, calls the BIOS video, keyboard or mouse interrupts (INT 10h, 16h, 33h) or draws through a function pointer, so it puts nothing in front of the player by itself. The 'strings' the first table listed are Ghidra labels of data-segment addresses that the code uses for pointer arithmetic (a structure field, the heap, a table), not text the routine writes; 3000:cdc9 for instance is Borland's far-heap allocator. Limit (as for the other internal rows): drawing through a far pointer to video memory that is held in a variable is not told apart.

Resource and picture loader: reads a record of the PRS file, decompresses or copies the bitmap rows into memory and tables (3000:4f53 sizes the block from the record's 0x20/0x22 fields, 3000:4abe reads the 14-byte header and the colour table, 3000:6587 and 3000:b0a7 build the colour/format tables, 1000:d955 keeps a table of loaded pictures). rows.shows: F10, the boss key: the screen goes to text mode with a DOS prompt "C:\>" in grey at its top left until a key is pressed, then the program's screen comes back
rows.how: The program's event loop FUN_2000_fd17 calls it on the key code 0x10c4 at any time: it hides the mouse, sets text mode (FUN_c000_233f with 3, 7 on a mono card), writes "C:\> " (DS 0x321), waits for a key, then sets the graphics mode again and repaints. Pressed F10 in the running original over the licence window: v20dos-orig-bosskey.png. Ours had no such key; the dos skin now shows a black page with "C:\>" in the screen font on F10 (bossKey), a key or a click brings the page back (looked at: v20dos-dg-boss.png). Traced (November 2026) on a disassembly of the unpacked image with the overlays' segment words resolved through the VROOMM segment table (docs/dos20-findings.md, "The 58 gap rows").
rows.diff: The prompt sits at the page's top left (the browser page is the screen) in the 8 x 14 screen font; text mode's own 8 x 16 font is not in the program's files.

rows.shows: Sets or reads the display mode, bank or palette of the video card.
rows.reason: Video-card layer: BIOS video calls (INT 10h; the VESA 4Fh functions: the card's mode list, set mode, bank switching) and the detection of the graphics card, 256-colour or monochrome (HOCOLOR.PRS or HOMONO.PRS, 3000:ac41). Read in decompiled/dos-2.0.1/all.c (private repo). A browser has no video modes or banks: the canvas is the screen; the colour pictures are shown, the monochrome ones are not offered (a kept difference of every skin).

rows.shows: The Ships menu's lines that change with the selection: "~Build Ships at %Fs..." / "Can't Build Ships Here..." (354/355), "~Review Battle at %Fs..." / "No Battles here..." (356/357), "~Organize Ships..." / "No ships to organize..." (358/359), "~Scrap Current Fleet" / "Don't ~Scrap Current Fleet" (360/361)
rows.how: The routine dims or enables each item and sets its words: Organize reads "No ships to organize..." and is dimmed when the selected star has nothing to organize (its field +0x30 is -1), Scrap reads "Don't ~Scrap Current Fleet" for a fleet marked for scrapping (+8), Review Battle names the star when its battle date is 2000 or later, Build names the star when it is the player's. Ours had every line but the dimmed Organize, which kept its enabled words; it now reads "No ships to organize…" when dimmed (menuLayoutDos, orgGhost; the words in ui-text.js in five languages). The others were already the original's (captured v20dos-orig-menu-s.png). rows.shows: F10, the boss key: the screen goes to text mode with a DOS prompt "C:\>" in grey at its top left until a key is pressed, then the program's screen comes back
rows.how: The program's event loop FUN_2000_fd17 calls it on the key code 0x10c4 at any time: it hides the mouse, sets text mode (FUN_c000_233f with 3, 7 on a mono card), writes "C:\> " (DS 0x321), waits for a key, then sets the graphics mode again and repaints. Pressed F10 in the running original over the licence window: v20dos-orig-bosskey.png. Ours had no such key; the dos skin now shows a black page with "C:\>" in the screen font on F10 (bossKey), a key or a click brings the page back (looked at: v20dos-dg-boss.png). Traced (November 2026) on a disassembly of the unpacked image with the overlays' segment words resolved through the VROOMM segment table (docs/dos20-findings.md, "The 58 gap rows").
rows.diff: The prompt sits at the page's top left (the browser page is the screen) in the 8 x 14 screen font; text mode's own 8 x 16 font is not in the program's files.

rows.shows: The Ships menu's lines that change with the selection: "~Build Ships at %Fs..." / "Can't Build Ships Here..." (354/355), "~Review Battle at %Fs..." / "No Battles here..." (356/357), "~Organize Ships..." / "No ships to organize..." (358/359), "~Scrap Current Fleet" / "Don't ~Scrap Current Fleet" (360/361)
rows.how: The routine dims or enables each item and sets its words: Organize reads "No ships to organize..." and is dimmed when the selected star has nothing to organize (its field +0x30 is -1), Scrap reads "Don't ~Scrap Current Fleet" for a fleet marked for scrapping (+8), Review Battle names the star when its battle date is 2000 or later, Build names the star when it is the player's. Ours had every line but the dimmed Organize, which kept its enabled words; it now reads "No ships to organize…" when dimmed (menuLayoutDos, orgGhost; the words in ui-text.js in five languages). The others were already the original's (captured v20dos-orig-menu-s.png). Traced (November 2026) on a disassembly of the unpacked image with the overlays' segment words resolved through the VROOMM segment table (docs/dos20-findings.md, "The 58 gap rows").

rows.shows: Sets or reads the display mode, bank or palette of the video card.

Read in decompiled/dos-2.0.1/all.c (private repo). A browser has no video modes or banks: the canvas is the screen; the colour pictures are shown, the monochrome ones are not offered (a kept difference of every skin).
